title: MTV VMAs: Does anyone even watch award ceremonies anymore?
description:
Madonna won Artist of the Year and Taylor Swift made a splash at Sunday’s MTV Video Music Awards - she became the most decorated performer in VMA history, and premiered her music video for Patient Zero, the lead single from the encore to her album The Life of a Showgirl.

And there’s a reason the VMAs might have been so keen to have her - award ceremonies aren’t pulling the big audiences that they used to. Millions of people used to tune in and pore over the outfits and the speeches, hoping their favourite artists would win. But now, viewing figures are falling for shows like the Grammys, the Oscars and the Emmys.

So… why are award shows in their flop era? And what’s being done to revive them?

BBC culture journalist William Lee Adams breaks it all down - and we hear from music fans on whether they think award ceremonies are still relevant.

summaryZh: 本集 BBC 節目《What in the World》探討 MTV 音樂錄影帶大獎等大型頒獎典禮收視率與文化影響力下滑的原因，以及主辦單位如何試圖重振榮景。節目分析指出，在社群媒體與串流平台普及的時代，大眾能隨時透過 TikTok 或 Spotify 關注明星動態，不再需要收看長達數小時的頒獎直播。為了挽救收視率， MTV 典禮除了邀請泰勒絲與瑪丹娜等巨星跨世代聯手創造話題，也透過與 CBS 電視網合作擴大播送範圍，試圖重塑頒獎典禮的流行文化影響力。
summaryEn: This episode of What in the World explores why major award ceremonies like the MTV Video Music Awards (VMAs), Grammys, and Oscars are suffering from declining viewership and reduced cultural impact. Host Hannah Gelbart and journalist William Lee Adams discuss how social media and streaming platforms provide 24/7 celebrity access, taking away the live television hype and fear of missing out. The episode highlights tactics used to revive interest, including leveraging major star power from Taylor Swift and Madonna, tapping into nostalgia, and expanding reach through broadcast partnerships with networks like CBS.
